title: KV prefix savings simulator (working)
summary: Working spreadsheet-style simulation exploring how prefix and KV cache hit-rate combinations translate to per-1M-token cost reductions across realistic request mixes. Focus is on sensitivity to prefix length distribution and hot-key skew.
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Quick experiment for product + infra to evaluate: if we improve prefix hit rates (or increase effective KV cache coverage), how much $/1M tokens do customers save? Which workloads benefit most?
- NOT final: this is a working simulator for discussion; assumes simple linear cost-per-token baseline for inference and a fixed marginal cost for KV cache hits.

Assumptions (editable parameters):
- Baseline model cost per token (hosted) = $0.000012 per token (12 microdollars)
- Backend CPU/ram + IO cost for serving 1 token from KV cache = $0.000003 per token (3 microdollars)
- Average response length (generation) = variable per scenario (50, 150, 400 tokens)
- Average prompt length (input) = variable; effective tokens billed = prompt + response in our usage model
- Caching definitions: prefix-hit = cached decoder context that avoids full forward pass for first N tokens; KV-hit = cache for key/value pairs reducing compute for next tokens after cache warm; we model combination as "effective hit" that reduces marginal tokens by 60% when prefix and KV both hit.
- Request mix buckets: short-chat (50 tokens), mid-chat (150 tokens), long-gen (400 tokens). Mix percentages are adjustable.

Key variables in sheet (columns):
- scenario_name
- mix_short_pct, mix_mid_pct, mix_long_pct
- avg_tokens_per_req (computed)
- prefix_hit_rate (0-1)
- kv_hit_rate (0-1)
- effective_hit_rate (computed as 1 - (1-prefix_hit_rate)*(1-kv_hit_rate)*0.4)  // heuristic: both misses reduce fewer tokens saved
- baseline_cost_per_1M = avg_tokens_per_req * baseline_token_cost * (1M / avg_tokens_per_req) => simplifies to 1M * baseline_token_cost
- cost_with_cache_per_1M = 1M * (baseline_token_cost*(1-effective_hit_rate) + cache_token_cost*effective_hit_rate)
- savings_per_1M = baseline_cost_per_1M - cost_with_cache_per_1M
- savings_pct = savings_per_1M / baseline_cost_per_1M

Small scenario matrix (examples):
CSV_TABLE_START
scenario,mix_short,mix_mid,mix_long,avg_tokens,prefix_hit,kv_hit,effective_hit,$/1M baseline,$/1M with cache,$ saved per 1M,saved %
chat-heavy,0.6,0.3,0.1,110,0.30,0.25,0.436,12000,7896,4104,34.2%
balanced,0.4,0.4,0.2,190,0.25,0.20,0.35,12000,9150,2850,23.8%
long-tail-gen,0.1,0.2,0.7,350,0.15,0.10,0.19,12000,10668,1332,11.1%
aggressive-cache,0.5,0.4,0.1,125,0.60,0.55,0.82,12000,4296,7704,64.2%

CSV_TABLE_END

Notes on the numbers above: baseline $/1M token simplifies to $12,000 because baseline token price = $0.000012 * 1,000,000 = $12,000. That makes outputs easier to reason about. Cache token cost uses assumed $0.000003. Effective_hit formula is intentionally conservative (we do NOT assume 100% compute saved even if prefix+kv both hit because some decode and routing still occurs).

Detailed worked example (chat-heavy row):
- avg tokens per request = 110 (derived from mix and per-bucket average).
- prefix_hit 30% and kv_hit 25% -> effective_hit ≈ 43.6% (heuristic).
- cost if no cache = 1,000,000 * 0.000012 = $12,000.
- cost with cache = 1,000,000 * (0.000012*(1-0.436) + 0.000003*0.436) = $7,896.
- savings = $4,104 (34.2%).

Sensitivity sections (editable in sheet):
- Vary baseline token cost: if baseline drops (cheaper model) relative value of cache decreases linearly. Add column: baseline_token_cost scenario multiplier.
- Cold vs warm cache: include a field for warm_fraction (portion of requests that hit a pre-warmed cache). If warm_fraction < 1, effective_hit = warm_fraction * effective_hit + (1-warm_fraction)*0.0 (approx).
- Hot-key skew: simulate Zipf distributions for prefix popularity. High skew -> small prefix set covers high fraction of traffic -> higher effective hit for same investment.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate cost of cache reads at scale with infra team (the $0.000003 value is a placeholder).
- Add per-model kernel costs: Llama-2-13B inference cost differs from Mistral/Redwood-custom. We should parameterize baseline_token_cost per model family.
- Evaluate difference between billing token model (prompt+resp) vs our internal compute-savings model — sometimes prompt tokens are cheaper to cache than generated tokens.
- Add simulation for batching synergy: caching + larger batch sizes may interact nonlinearly; initial model assumes independence.
- Graphs to add: savings vs prefix_hit at fixed kv_hit; savings heatmap (prefix_hit x kv_hit).

Quick action list (for next meeting):
- [ ] Confirm cache read marginal cost with infra (ENG-7450) by 2025-07-10 (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Add model-specific baseline token rates (owner: Sofia) — repo PR: PR#4821.
- [ ] Run Zipf distribution experiments on production traces (owner: Maya) to estimate realistic prefix skew.

Appendix: short pseudo-code for simulator (to copy into a notebook)
- parameters: baseline_token_cost, cache_token_cost, bucket_avgs, bucket_mix, prefix_hit, kv_hit, warm_fraction
- compute avg_tokens = sum(bucket_avgs * bucket_mix)
- effective_hit = warm_fraction * (1 - (1-prefix_hit)*(1-kv_hit)*0.4)
- cost_with_cache_1M = 1_000_000 * (baseline_token_cost*(1-effective_hit) + cache_token_cost*effective_hit)
- return savings

References / context links:
- Design doc: confluence:kv-cache-design (linked above)
- ENG ticket for infra cost estimate: ENG-7450
- Prior analysis: product/optimize/kv-prefix-econ-scenarios-q1-2026.json (use only for high-level cross-checks; this sheet aims to be more experimental and notebook-friendly)

Notes-to-self (loose):
- Might want to separate "prefix" vs "kv" more clearly: prefix = reuse of entire prefix logits/cache so that decode skip is higher; KV = token-level KV-cache that speeds subsequent attention. In practice terming is fuzzy across infra.
- Keep the simulator as a small sheet + python notebook. Avoid overfitting to a single baseline price.

End of working sheet.
